summary: Markets are navigating a cautiously optimistic but geopolitically charged environment, with sentiment buoyed by diplomatic progress on multiple Middle Eastern fronts even as underlying tensions remain elevated. The potential Strait of Hormuz deal, flagged by Treasury Secretary Bessent as possibly imminent this week, is the dominant macro catalyst, sending oil prices sharply lower with Goldman Sachs projecting Brent in the $80–$90 range pending resolution of the US-Iran conflict, while Asia crude imports recovering but remaining below pre-war levels underscores the lasting supply disruption. At the stock level, Palantir surged 16% on record commercial AI revenue, Pfizer beat quarterly estimates and raised guidance on non-Covid product strength, and SpaceX is generating significant speculative interest on Wall Street, while Chipotle shares fell on a salmonella outbreak investigation in Minnesota. Key risks investors are monitoring include the US having depleted virtually all long-range precision missiles during the Iran war — raising escalation uncertainty — ongoing Houthi attacks in the Red Sea region, Black Sea drone threats disrupting grain and energy corridors, and Iran's demand for inbound Hormuz control, which could complicate any deal. The short-term outlook hinges almost entirely on whether a Hormuz agreement materializes this week, with a successful deal likely triggering further oil price declines and a broader risk-on rally, while any breakdown in negotiations or fresh military escalation could rapidly reverse current gains.
